title: Hardship and Protective Holds: Recertification and the Review Package Standard
content:
**Standard.** Under Hardship and Protective Holds, the date an updated physician's medical or disability certification on a running Long-Term Hardship Hold is due on depends on the hold's review history — the number of status reviews recorded on the hold as continuing it:

| Reviews recorded as continuing the hold | The recertification is due on |
|---|---|
| Two or more | The due date of the latest income records request on the hold, so that both arrive as one review package |
| Exactly one | The later of that income records due date and the last day of the review's overdue window |
| None yet | The last day of the review's overdue window |

**Terms.**

- *The latest income records request on the hold* is the most recent documentation request for household income records in the hold's history; its due date is the date that request set.
- *The review's overdue window* belongs to the review the recertification is for: the next status review to fall due after the day of the request, a review falling due on the day of the request counting as already fallen due. Reviews of this tier fall due every 60 calendar days counted from the hold's start date, and the window's last day is 15 calendar days after that review's due date.
- The days allowed for the recertification are the calendar days from the day of the request to the date so found.

## Branches worked through (hypothetical)

A hold started on 1 March; reviews fall due on 30 April, 29 June and 28 August. The request is made on 20 June, so the review it is for falls due on 29 June and its overdue window ends on 14 July.

| Continuing reviews | Latest income records due date | Due date of the recertification | Days allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 20 July | 20 July | 30 |
| 1 | 20 July | 20 July (later than 14 July) | 30 |
| 1 | 10 July | 14 July (later than 10 July) | 24 |
| 0 | 20 July | 14 July | 24 |
